t:
(a) 
None of the funds available to the Department  of Defense for any fiscal year for drug interdiction or counter-drug activities may be transferred to any other department or agency of the United States except as specifically provided in an appropriations law.
 
    (b) 
None of the funds available to the Central Intelligence  Agency for any fiscal year for drug interdiction and counter-drug activities may be transferred to any other department or agency of the United States except as specifically provided in an appropriations law.

fable.w: This section only restricts transfers of drug interdiction funds between federal departments and agencies unless an appropriations law provides otherwise. The tempting reading is that references to other departments or agencies imply coordination, but every actor is inside the federal government and no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, or right to sue is created. No outside party is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: None of the funds available to the Department  of Defense for any fiscal year for drug interdiction or counter-drug activities may be transferred to any other department or agency of the United States except as specifically provided in an appropriations law.

qwen_block.w: This section restricts the transfer of funds between federal agencies (Department of Defense, CIA, and other departments/agencies). It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation with any entities outside the federal government, such as states, tribes, the public, or private organizations. The actors involved are entirely within the federal government.
qwen_block.s: None of the funds available to the Department of Defense for any fiscal year for drug interdiction or counter-drug activities may be transferred to any other department or agency of the United States except as specifically provided in an appropriations law.

opus.w: This section only limits transfers of counter-drug funds from DoD and the CIA to other federal agencies. The only exception is an act of Congress, and Congress is inside the federal government. No outside party consults on, comments on, or can challenge any federal decision, so the 'appropriations law' exception does not count as participation.
opus.s: None of the funds available to the Department  of Defense for any fiscal year for drug interdiction or counter-drug activities may be transferred to any other department or agency of the United States except as specifically provided in an appropriations law.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** The exception "except as specifically provided in an appropriations law" might look like an outside party having a say over the transfers. It isn't one. Only Congress can pass an appropriations law, and Congress is inside the federal government. The section is just a limit on moving funds between federal agencies. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and no one gets a hearing, comment period or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section restricts the transfer of funds between federal agencies (Department of Defense, Central Intelligence Agency, and other US departments/agencies). All entities involved are inside the federal government. There is no requirement to consult with or coordinate with any outside parties (such as states, tribes, or the public) before making a decision. Therefore, it does not involve participation as defined.
qwen_chat.s: None of the funds available to the Department of Defense for any fiscal year for drug interdiction or counter-drug activities may be transferred to any other department or agency of the United States except as specifically provided in an appropriations law.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions "drug interdiction" and "counter-drug activities," it implies some form of public engagement or consultation with external entities. However, the text strictly limits the *transfer of funds* between federal agencies (DoD, CIA, and other US departments/agencies). All actors mentioned (DoD, CIA, other US departments/agencies) are inside the federal government. There is no requirement to consult with states, tribes, the public, or private entities.
